statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains below the block threshold while bond, oil, and geopolitical Stress remains extreme.
recommendation: Current conditions are assessed as low Tail with extreme Stress; the main conditional checkpoint is the U.S. cash-open and state-employment release window.
headline: Overnight Nasdaq futures stabilize while high yields, oil and Hormuz disruption keep Stress extreme
body: Nasdaq and S&P futures were modestly firmer in Asian trading after Thursday's selloff, while the U.S. 10-year yield remained near 4.71% and Brent near $93.5. Strait of Hormuz commodity-vessel crossings fell to seven on Thursday. With no fresh verified persistent one-way NQ continuation, Tail remains low.

U.S. premarket participation increases. Prior-session megacap weakness remains relevant, but mixed semiconductor context limits confidence in a uniform downside path.
Approaching the U.S. opening sequence, event and auction uncertainty lift Tail to WATCH. Direction remains conditional on actual pre-open structure rather than the calendar alone.
The 15:00 Berlin hour approaches the 15:30 cash open. Tail is WATCH if Thursday's downside reasserts with shallow retracements; an orderly open would argue for decay.
The 16:00 Berlin hour includes State Employment and Unemployment after the cash open. Tail peaks at 24%; crossing 25% requires observed persistent directional efficiency.
After the state-labor release, Tail remains WATCH only if the first-hour move extends with weak retracements. Two-sided price discovery would support faster normalization.
Late morning U.S. trade should clarify whether opening pressure persists. Failure to extend and improving breadth would reduce Tail while oil and yields can keep Stress high.
Midday liquidity can weaken directional efficiency. Tail stays WATCH only if NQ continues to hold near downside extremes and rebounds repeatedly fail.
Early afternoon is modeled below WATCH if the session develops meaningful retracements. Renewed cross-asset downside alignment would be the main re-escalation condition.
Power-hour approach raises continuation sensitivity modestly. Tail returns to WATCH only if an established directional move is still extending without meaningful pullback.
Cash-close price discovery can amplify a persistent trend, but the forecast remains conditional. A balanced close would leave Tail below the block threshold.
CME equity-index futures are expected to enter the weekend closure after Friday trading ends. With no live NQ path, headline risk remains Stress rather than observed Tail structure.
During the weekend closure, no live NQ continuation can be observed. Tail stays low while geopolitical and oil headlines remain potential reopening-gap drivers.
Weekend closure continues. Without futures price discovery, current market-path claims are unavailable; Stress remains elevated because Hormuz and bond-market risks are unresolved.

Saturday closed-market conditions limit path inference. Geopolitical escalation would primarily raise reopening Stress until live NQ price discovery resumes.
Weekend closure persists; no future one-way price structure is assumed. Tail remains low unless new verified discontinuities materially change the reopening risk profile.
With NQ closed, the forecast emphasizes headline and gap uncertainty rather than directional efficiency. Existing oil and fiscal-rate stress remains the main background risk.
The final forecast hour remains within the weekend closure. Tail stays low because no live failed-retracement path can be observed; reopening risk depends on later verified developments.
